focus: evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review
standards: Michigan HESG 2025 Grades 9-12 [12.3.PHW] Personal Health and Wellness — Information and Resource Seeking

standards_mapping.framework: Michigan Health Education Standards Guidelines 2025 (grades 9-12 band)
standards_mapping.practice: Michigan Health Practice 3: Information and Resource Seeking
standards_mapping.note: Practice name and topic abbreviation verified against the official source; the band code follows the confirmed <terminal-grade>.<practice>.<TOPIC> pattern. No per-indicator number is claimed.

essential_question: What separates a health claim that holds up from one that only sounds like it does?
learning_objectives: Explain evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review accurately using current, reliable health information rather than assumption or anecdote.
Apply evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review inside a fictional scenario, showing the reasoning, evidence, or decision process that produced the response.
Check and revise the work on evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review against stated success criteria and name the next step.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review without being asked for any private disclosure.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a documented process, or a cited source rather than an unsupported claim.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: course-supplied fictional product and service descriptions

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short accessible prompt on “evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review.” Ask the learner to recall, predict, or pose a question before instruction. Use a fictional example; do not ask about the learner's own situation.

Teach accurate, age-appropriate content on evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review. Model the health skill in play — analyzing an influence, evaluating a source, running a decision, communicating a boundary, or identifying a trusted support — and name the success criteria.

Work two supported scenarios about evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review together. After each, ask what evidence or reasoning supports the move. Fade prompting on the second scenario.

Learner applies evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review to a new fictional scenario and records the response together with the reasoning, evidence, or decision process behind it.

In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review, then name one check that would catch a weak claim or an unsafe step.

student_activity: Learner applies evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review to a new fictional scenario and records the response with the reasoning, evidence, or decision process behind it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review, then name one check that would catch a weak claim or an unsafe step.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches that meet the criteria. Never score body size, appearance, personal circumstances, or willingness to disclose. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh scenario.
Ask the learner to explain why the approach to evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied scenario about evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short later review.
Do not record it, do not treat it as assessment evidence, and route the learner to a trusted adult or qualified professional. Continue the lesson with the fictional scenario.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use scenario response, decision process, communication practice, safety plan, and private or minimally disclosive reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or representation.
extension: Apply evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
Evaluations may be written, tabled, dictated, or completed against a supplied criteria rubric with a reduced item count.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Do not require disclosure of private health, trauma, diagnosis, body, or family information.
Use body-respect language; do not use dieting, calorie targets, weight cutting, weigh-ins, or body-size scoring.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, calorie counts, diet goals, medical history, mental-health diagnosis, or sexual history at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; every task has a text, spoken-to-an-adult, or demonstrated alternative.
This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.
No purchase, account creation, real product order, payment information, or personal health-product use is requested or recorded.

guardian_safety.equipment: None. No purchase is required at any point.
guardian_safety.sensitive_content_note: All products and services evaluated are fictional course artifacts.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, source excerpt, worked example, or short clip supporting evidence hierarchy in plain language: anecdote, observation, trial, review.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, a transcript, or an adult explanation. No lesson requires media to be completed.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw reflections, raw answers, recordings, body data, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical or sensitive-content units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
